A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CULTDIFF and CULTDIFF-S. Their main text, equations, three tables, 17 figures and appendices are readable and matchable despite pagination and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original human evaluations involving 30 annotators across ten countries, comparisons of diffusion-generated images, and learned similarity-metric results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, human-evaluation and similarity-metric results, including the appendix survey analyses, and adds qualitative findings about generation failures.

M1.justification: The image-pair construction, human-score threshold, ViT contrastive learning, weighted margin loss and cosine-similarity scoring remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 newly specifies implementation details without establishing a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten countries and architecture, clothing and food categories. The new failure-pattern discussion examines existing coverage; newly cited benchmarks are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate SD-XL, SD-3-Medium and FLUX.1-dev, and compare CULTDIFF-S against FID, LPIPS and SSIM, printed as SISM in Table 2. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The survey design, 30 annotators, five-point scale, 30/10/10 prompt split and approximately 11k/2.7k/2.7k image-pair counts are retained. Appendix A.2 discloses previously unspecified settings; it does not report changes to existing protocols.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.6 adds a brief qualitative error analysis covering Azerbaijani clothing, Ethiopian architecture, Korean clothing and Pakistani food. Existing prompt-choice observations and survey-correlation analyses remain unchanged; no controlled ablation is added.

E5.justification: Section 4.1.2 newly reports that differences between overrepresented and underrepresented countries are not statistically significant, adding an explicit uncertainty qualification. No test specification or p-values accompany it; existing standard-error bars and Fleiss' Kappa reporting remain.

E6.justification: v2 adds qualitative cultural-confusion findings in Appendix A.6 and the textual nonsignificance finding in Section 4.1.2. Numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged, including CULTDIFF-S's Spearman correlation of 0.1848 and Pearson correlation of 0.1559 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The weighted margin-loss equation and its definitions are mathematically unchanged; added multiplication symbols and formatting are equivalent. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the ten-country benchmark, cultural-disparity claims and human-feedback-trained similarity metric. The added qualifications in the results discussion do not revise these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 suggests that nonsignificant group differences reflect the small dataset and that low annotator agreement may reflect evaluation of different model outputs. It also emphasizes variation in country rankings across models and discusses specific cultural confusions in Appendix A.6.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.2 supplies generator parameter counts and specifies ViT-Base's architecture, 10 training epochs, learning rate 1e-4, batch size 32 and 224-by-224 image resolution. These are newly disclosed details of the existing implementation.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds six cited works covering image transcreation, culturally aware captioning, CulText2I, C3, CVQA and cultural bias in AI. This broadens related-work coverage while retaining the paper's positioning around underrepresented cultures.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited language corrections, adds explanatory passages and two appendix topics, and renumbers the survey appendices. Affiliations, author notes and acknowledgments are expanded, while the main section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 17 figures and three tables are retained, with unchanged figure-image content and table structures. Displays are redistributed across pages, and Table 3's caption is revised to describe agreement across diffusion models.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.2 improves reproducibility through concrete model and training details, while the failure analysis and additional qualifications improve transparency. The gains are limited: the nonsignificance statement lacks test details or p-values, and the abstract still describes significant disparities. The revision provides useful clarification without resolving the study's underlying evidential limitations.
